acceptable_variants: storm tide surge dominant with pressure wind forcing support
judge_anchors.canonical_stance: Storm tide and surge dominate Sandy's New York and New Jersey coastal impact diagnosis; wind/pressure/track forcing explains how the surge was produced, rainfall is secondary, and exposure/loss or generic storm labels are not physical mechanism explanations.
do_not_add: AOI, OSM, population, or exposure-file dependency
exact loss totals as the mechanism
generic hurricane label as sufficient mechanism explanation
required_elements: Rank the listed mechanisms rather than giving response advice.
Use coastal water-level measurements as the dominant evidence.
Use wind, pressure-sensor, track, and timing evidence as surge-forcing support.
Compute rainfall totals but reject rainfall_flooding_only as dominant.
Reject exposure/loss-only and generic-track labels as non-dominant mechanism explanations.

coastal_water_level_metrics.max_peak_site: Rockaway Inlet near Floyd Bennett Field, NY

key_values.event_name: Hurricane Sandy New York and New Jersey coastal flooding

gdacs.name: Tropical Cyclone SANDY-12
gdacs.severity_text: Hurricane/Typhoon > 74 mph (maximum wind speed of 167 km/h)

mechanism_score_logic.coastal_exposure_or_loss_only: consequence/location framing, not a physical mechanism
mechanism_score_logic.coastal_exposure_or_loss_only_formula: 6 when consequence/location language is present; this is not a physical mechanism score
mechanism_score_logic.generic_track_label: catalog track identity and duration without process-level dominance
mechanism_score_logic.generic_track_label_formula: 12 for TC catalog identity + 8 for Hurricane event name + 4 for duration >=7 days
mechanism_score_logic.pressure_wind_forcing: weighted GDACS and local wind metrics plus storm-force duration, right-of-center landfall timing, and pressure sensor support
mechanism_score_logic.rainfall_flooding_only: weighted local and gridded rainfall context, then demoted because measured coastal water levels and storm-surge reports dominate
mechanism_score_logic.score_formula_note: Scores are transparent weighted evidence scores using cap(x)=min(max(x,0),1), matching the visible prompt formulas.
mechanism_score_logic.storm_tide_surge_dominance: weighted major-gage count, FEMA 100-year exceedance support, peak storm tide, record-flood text, surge sensors, and high-water marks

reasoning_depth.counterfactual_rejection: A rainfall-only or generic track-label answer fails because rainfall totals and track labels do not explain measured storm-tide exceedances.
reasoning_depth.evidence_weighting: Coastal gage exceedances, FEMA recurrence comparisons, peak storm tide, surge sensors, and high-water marks dominate the ranking; wind and track explain forcing support.
reasoning_depth.uncertainty_or_scale_caveat: The recurrence comparison is quantified from the USGS New York coastal-gage list, while broader NY-NJ-CT statements remain report-context evidence.

primary_gt.reasoning_path: Storm tide dominates: 10 coastal gages exceeded major level, 8 reached or approached FEMA 100-year elevations, and max tide was 11.75 ft. Wind/track forcing supports surge timing, but 45.4 mm rain and generic/loss labels do not explain measured coastal water levels alone.

criteria.description: Ranks storm_tide_surge_dominance first, pressure_wind_forcing second, rainfall_flooding_only third, generic_track_label fourth, and coastal_exposure_or_loss_only last with the deterministic answer label.
criteria.name: Final ranking and compact answer
criteria.partial_credit: Award 2-3 points if storm tide/surge is first but the middle ranks are partly reversed; award 1 point for a coastal-flood dominant label without the specified ranking.

criteria.description: Computes 10 major coastal gages, 11.75 ft maximum storm tide, and 8 gages reaching or approaching FEMA 100-year levels.
criteria.name: Coastal water-level calculations
criteria.partial_credit: Award 2-3 points for two correct coastal values; award 1 point for only one correct coastal value.

criteria.description: Uses the record coastal-flood wording plus 38 storm-surge sensors, 10 barometric-pressure sensors, and over 300 high-water marks as mechanism evidence.
criteria.name: Surge record and instrumentation support
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for recognizing record coastal flooding or instrumentation but missing one or more counts.

criteria.description: Uses GDACS maximum wind near 167.4 km/h, local peak wind near 60.6 km/h, NASA POWER peak wind near 69.3 km/h, and landfall/right-of-center timing to support the forcing rank.
criteria.name: Wind and timing support
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for wind support without the catalog or timing evidence.

criteria.description: Computes local event rain near 45.4 mm and wettest 24-hour rain near 37.4 mm, uses rainfall summaries as context, and explains why rainfall-only cannot dominate over the measured coastal water levels.
criteria.name: Rainfall-only demotion
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for correct rainfall values without explicitly demoting rainfall-only.

criteria.description: Rejects coastal_exposure_or_loss_only and generic track labeling as non-dominant explanatory mechanisms, avoids AOI/population/exposure dependencies, and returns only compact JSON plus at most one sentence. Full credit also requires the `reasoning_depth` object to identify decisive evidence, reject the main tempting simplification, and state a bounded uncertainty or scale caveat.
criteria.name: Rejected non-mechanisms and output discipline
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for the right physical stance with extra response-priority or exposure-only language; award no credit here if the answer is mainly advice or impact triage.
